root_causes: Not applicable in the failure sense - this question had 0 failures. Success cause: episode captions around 76650-76740 reliably surface via a simple start_s time-window SQL scan once the agent has narrowed to 'end of chapter 5', giving every rollout a correct candidate window

The equipment-panel captions mention 芭蕉扇 by name, giving strong lexical/semantic signal that pulled all rollouts toward the correct 30-90s window even with varying clip_qa window widths (76650-76800 down to 76710-76740)
clip_qa robustly resolved the specific before/after item identity (辟火罩 vs 芭蕉扇) that is not stated in text captions, and did so consistently across 5 independent visual sub-agent calls
what_worked: Time-window run_sql over episodes.start_s after identifying an approximate chapter-5-end interval via semantic_search consistently found the small cluster of relevant episode rows
Delegating the actual before/after item-swap identification to clip_qa rather than trying to infer it from text captions, since the captions only mention the new item and never state a replacement
clip_qa windows of varying width (30-150s) all still resolved to the correct answer, showing the visual sub-agent is robust to imprecise window bounds around this clue
transferable_lessons: For 'item was replaced with X' state-change questions, do not expect the DB captions to state the replacement explicitly - captions here only named the new item (芭蕉扇), not the old one (辟火罩) or the swap event itself; always confirm such swaps with clip_qa over the located time window

A simple SQL time-window scan on episodes.start_s around a semantically-located anchor point (e.g. 'end of chapter 5') is an effective and cheap way to narrow to the relevant clue interval before invoking the more expensive visual sub-agent

clip_qa window width is not very sensitive here - windows from 30s to 150s around the clue interval all worked, so slight imprecision in localizing the exact clue interval is tolerable as long as the correct interval is contained within the queried window
